title: RagGAD: Rationale-Aware Conditional Gaussian Mixture Normalizing Flow for Unsupervised Graph Anomaly Detection
abstract: arXiv:2608.16018v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Graph anomaly detection aims to identify nodes that deviate from normal behavioral patterns within graphs. However, existing methods largely rely on the homophily assumption, which makes it difficult to distinguish spurious affinities and to capture the diverse behaviors of normal nodes,limiting their robustness in complex real-world scenarios. To address this problem, we propose RagGAD, an unsupervised graph anomaly detection framework based on rationale-aware conditional Gaussian mixture normalizing flow. RagGAD introduces an adaptive rationale disentangler to disentangle stable rationales from spurious correlations within node interrelationships, and further decomposes stable rationales into robust and fragile components. The learned rationales capture underlying interaction patterns that characterize normal behaviors under varying conditions, while anomalies emerge as deviations associated with unstable or spurious correlations. translated_title: RagGAD：基于理性感知的条件高斯混合归一化流的无监督图异常检测
translated_abstract: 图异常检测旨在识别图中偏离正常行为模式的节点。然而，现有方法主要依赖于同质性假设，这使得难以区分虚假关联并捕捉正常节点的多样化行为，从而限制了它们在复杂现实场景中的鲁棒性。为解决这一问题，我们提出了RagGAD，一种基于理性感知的条件高斯混合归一化流的无监督图异常检测框架。RagGAD引入了一个自适应理性解耦器，用于将节点相互关系中的稳定理性与虚假相关性解耦，并进一步将稳定理性分解为稳健和脆弱组件。学习到的理性捕捉了在不同条件下表征正常行为的潜在交互模式，而异常则表现为与不稳定或虚假相关性相关的偏差。
tldr: 本文提出RagGAD框架，通过自适应理性解耦器分离稳定与虚假关联，并分解为稳健和脆弱组件，从而在无监督条件下有效检测图异常，克服了同质性假设的局限性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes RagGAD, a framework that uses an adaptive rationale disentangler to separate stable and spurious correlations, decomposing rationales into robust and fragile components, enabling effective unsupervised graph anomaly detection beyond homophily assumptions.
